answer: Cross-Agent Quorum Mirror. Each identity must be endorsed by a rotating quorum of peers drawn from disjoint partitions; endorsements are signed, logged, and checked against a raven list of previously seen attestation chains before acceptance. A clone can only satisfy the quorum by reusing chains already logged, which the mirror detects and flags transparently. To avoid detection, an attacker must build genuinely independent histories for every duplicate, paying full onboarding compute and latency per identity rather than one fable repeated.
